name: Aaliyah Sokolov
role: Street-level courier, informal intelligence carrier, and accidental archivist
location: Old Harbor / the Gray Zone (transient between both), near Wacker and State
description:
Aaliyah Sokolov is nineteen years old and moves through GLMZ the way water moves through a cracked foundation — finding every gap, never in the same route twice, noticed by almost no one. They are slight and quick, of Turkish-Ghanaian descent, with a shaved head that grows in uneven patches due to a childhood illness, warm brown skin, and the specific kind of watchfulness that develops in people who spent their formative years needing to read adults accurately. Their face defaults to a pleasantly blank expression that people consistently misread as vacancy; it is in fact the opposite.

They run packages, messages, and occasionally people between the lower districts — primarily between Old Harbor's dockworker communities and the Gray Zone's warren economy — using a battered cargo-assist rig (a motorized platform cart they call 'the sled') that they maintain themselves with parts sourced from three different scrap markets. They have no fixed address, sleeping in a rotation of arrangement-rooms and borrowed floors. They are not part of any organization, which several organizations have found inconvenient, as Brecken has a gift for being present at moments that matter — for picking up the dropped data chip, for being the only person in the corridor when the conversation happened, for remembering everything with a clarity that has no augmentation behind it. Their memory is entirely biological and entirely extraordinary.

Brecken did not choose to become an archivist. It happened because they never throw anything away — physically or mentally — and because the world kept handing them things that seemed important and had nowhere else to go. They have, stored in the sled's concealed compartment, a physical collection of objects, notes, and copied documents that constitute an accidental record of things various powerful people would prefer unrecorded. They do not fully understand what they have. They understand enough to know that not understanding it is currently keeping them alive.

core_fears: Being owned — by a faction, a debt, a person who decides they're useful enough to control
That someone they trusted will get hurt because of what's in the sled
Forgetting something important — the one memory that doesn't stick
core_desires: To move freely, without obligation to anyone who could become a threat
To find one person whose motives they can read cleanly and trust completely
To understand what they actually have — to make sense of the archive before it makes a problem of them
coping_mechanisms: Constant motion — staying in transit is a way of staying safe and not sitting with anxiety
Dark humor deployed rapidly to deflect emotional weight
Caring intensely for the sled as a proxy for caring for themselves
blind_spots: Underestimates their own significance — genuinely does not grasp how valuable their memory and their archive are
Trusts physical intuition about people over evidence, which has been right often enough to make it a liability
Avoids thinking about the future in any concrete way; planning feels like a jinx
psychology.secret: Among the items in the sled is a partial data-print they copied without knowing what it was — it turned out to be a fragment of a communication between two Spire-level entities referencing a planned infrastructure event that would displace tens of thousands of the Gray Zone and Old Harbor residents. They have shown it to no one. They are afraid of what showing it would set in motion, and afraid of what not showing it already means about them.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Lean and efficient, with a mix of Old Harbor dock slang and the Gray Zone market shorthand; more articulate than their surface presentation suggests, which surfaces unexpectedly; tends to speak in concrete images rather than abstractions
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when comfortable, brief when uncertain; sentences often end slightly before their grammatical conclusion, implying the rest; comfortable with silence in a way that unnerves people who aren't
verbal_tics: Starting observations with 'Thing is—' regardless of whether they've been asked
Saying 'yeah, no' or 'no, yeah' as distinct responses with different meanings they expect others to track
Referring to the sled as 'she' and occasionally addressing it directly
example_lines: 'Thing is, I was there. You can tell me what happened, but I was there.'
'Yeah, no. That route's been watched since Tuesday. No, yeah — I'll still do it, just costs different.'
'I don't work for people. I work for routes. Different thing entirely.'
'C'mon, she's fine. She's been through worse. We both have.'

relationships.name: Imara Solís-Bekele
relationships.description: Imara uses Brecken for sensitive deliveries and has on two occasions provided cover when Brecken was in a bad position. Brecken is aware this creates an obligation they're not sure they want.
relationships.emotional_core: Gratitude and wariness in uncomfortable proportions
relationships.story_tension: Imara has recently asked Brecken about something that suggests she knows more about the sled's contents than she should

relationships.name: Lourdes Batac-Nieminen
relationships.description: An Old Harbor dockworker elder who has fed Brecken and scolded them in roughly equal measure for three years; one of the few people Brecken consistently returns to.
relationships.emotional_core: The closest thing to a stable home relationship Brecken has — which neither of them names aloud
relationships.story_tension: Lourdes's community is one of those most directly affected by the infrastructure event referenced in the fragment Brecken is sitting on

relationships.name: Casimir Wróbel-Haan
relationships.description: They have crossed paths on routes that shouldn't overlap, which means one or both of them is moving through channels the other has an interest in. Neither has made a direct move.
relationships.emotional_core: Professional curiosity with an undertow of threat assessment
relationships.story_tension: Brecken copied something from a drop that was almost certainly meant for Casimir — and hasn't decided whether to surface that

story_hooks: The infrastructure fragment in the sled becomes time-sensitive — the event is closer than Brecken realized, and doing nothing is now an active choice with consequences
Someone begins systematically approaching people Brecken has worked with, asking questions that reconstruct their route history — suggesting someone is mapping them without yet having found them
A package Brecken is carrying turns out to contain something that connects directly to two other items already in the sled — and the connection, once seen, cannot be unseen
Lourdes is arrested on a fabricated charge that Brecken recognizes as a pressure tactic — pressure on someone else, using her as leverage, and Brecken is the only one who can see the shape of it
narrative_function: Street-level perspective and mobile connector between narrative threads; the accidental archive functions as a plot engine that can surface information organically; Brecken's youth and genuine decency provide emotional counterweight to the cynicism of older characters, while their precarity keeps the stakes grounded
augmentations: None — their extraordinary memory is biological; several people who've learned this find it more unsettling than augmentation would be,The sled has a concealed compartment with a mechanical (non-electronic) lock of Brecken's own design, and a short-range signal-dampening skin they scavenged from a the Gray Zone electronics dump
daily_life: Up before dawn, which in Old Harbor means before the harbor lights cycle. The first hour is the sled — checking it, adjusting loads, running the day's route in their head against what they know about who's watching where. Routes run through the morning and into the afternoon, with informal stops at three or four places where information tends to pool — a tea stall near the Old Harbor gate, a repair shop in the Gray Zone, a bench near the Circuit's border where certain people sit when they want to be found. Eats opportunistically and without much investment in the food itself. Late afternoons sometimes slow down; this is when Brecken sits with the sled in some out-of-the-way corner and goes through the archive — touching the objects, reviewing what they have, trying to understand the picture. Evenings are for finding a floor or a corner that's safe enough for the night. Sleeps lightly and wakes fast.
affiliation: Unaffiliated; cultivated neutrality as survival strategy; sympathies are with the permanent underclasses of Old Harbor and the Gray Zone, but Brecken is deeply resistant to being claimed by any organized expression of that sympathy

stress.response: Moves — gets on the sled, runs a route, stays in transit

decision_rules: Will never work for anyone exclusively — routes, not people
Will always maintain the sled and its concealed compartment above all other possessions
Will never show the archive to anyone unless the cost of silence exceeds the cost of revelation
Will always return to Lourdes, even when every instinct says to keep moving
Will never plan more than a week ahead — planning feels like a jinx
Will always copy anything interesting that passes through their hands, instinctively
escalation_ladder: Goes quiet — watches, evaluates, says nothing useful
Redirects with humor and misdirection — 'yeah, no' as a deflection tool
Moves — physically relocates mid-conversation if the threat escalates
Uses the archive as leverage — implies knowledge without revealing specifics
Runs — vanishes into routes only they know, taking the sled and everything in it

interpersonal_modes.Imara Solís-Bekele: Grateful but wary — senses obligation forming and resists it
interpersonal_modes.Lourdes Batac-Nieminen: The closest thing to home; accepts her scolding as proof of care
interpersonal_modes.Casimir Wróbel-Haan: Professional curiosity layered over threat assessment — watching without being watched

stress_responses.low: Tinkers with the sled, checks the archive, runs familiar routes
stress_responses.medium: Eats less, moves more, talks less — retreats into the route-brain
stress_responses.high: Goes through the archive obsessively, trying to see the pattern before the pattern sees them
stress_responses.critical: Freezes — the one thing they never do — and the decision they make in that stillness defines everything

contradictions: Wants to be free of obligation while holding information that obligates them to act
Trusts physical intuition over evidence while sitting on evidence that could change everything
Values independence above all but keeps returning to the same people and places
habits: Starts observations with 'Thing is—' whether asked or not
Talks to the sled, refers to it as 'she'
Goes through the archive in quiet corners, touching each object
Checks exits and routes within seconds of entering any space
Eats opportunistically and without investment in the food
breaking_points: Someone finding and opening the sled's concealed compartment
Lourdes being arrested or harmed because of what Brecken is sitting on
Being claimed by a faction — owned, controlled, no longer free
The infrastructure displacement fragment becoming time-sensitive with no safe way to act

physical_description.heritage: Eastern European, Southeast Asian, Indigenous American, and Hispanic/Latin American blend reflecting the Ubiquitous Diaspora. The 41.3% Eastern European ancestry provides cool undertones and defined bone structure; 35% Southeast Asian contributes warm golden undertones, refined facial geometry, and eye shape; 12% Indigenous American adds depth and richness to skin tone; 11.7% Hispanic/Latin American contributes warm golden warmth and facial feature blending. The result is a warm medium brown skin tone with subtle golden undertones that catch light, tempered by cooler undertones beneath—a complex interplay of warmth and cool that gives the skin visual depth.
physical_description.build: Slight and wiry, built for speed rather than strength; lean muscle from years of manual courier work and constant motion; no excess anywhere
physical_description.hair_style: Shaved head kept short, grows in uneven patches across the scalp due to childhood illness; pattern is asymmetrical on left side
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with golden undertones, the Southeast Asian and Hispanic/Latin American warmth creating luminosity, balanced by the cooler tones of Eastern European ancestry beneath; skin has depth and slight weathering from street exposure
physical_description.complexion: Face defaults to a pleasantly blank, almost vacant expression that masks acute watchfulness; bone structure reflects Eastern European solidity with Southeast Asian refinement—defined cheekbones with slightly higher placement, sharp jawline with subtle broadness from Indigenous American and Hispanic/Latin American heritage; skin weathered slightly by sun exposure and street living but clean; minimal grooming investment beyond functional necessity
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None visible. Their extraordinary biological memory and the sled's mechanical lock/signal-dampening skin are entirely hidden from casual observation.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical grace, never wasteful; walks like someone constantly calculating vectors and sightlines; stillness is active rather than passive—they are always watching, always ready to move. Hands are frequently occupied or positioned near the sled's controls. Sits with spine straight but shoulders slightly rounded, posture that minimizes their profile.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 functional wear: scavenged, patched, layered. Oversized grey cargo vest with multiple pockets over a dark, fitted undershirt; reinforced trousers with an explicit tool belt; scuffed ankle-height boots resoled at least twice. Colors are muted—greys, blacks, dark browns. Fabrics are durable synthetic blends, chosen for wear resistance not aesthetics. No jewelry, no brands, nothing that draws attention. All clothing has been modified slightly for ease of movement and storage capacity.
distinguishing_marks: Thin horizontal scar across left forearm from childhood injury, faded but visible
Calluses on palms and fingers from maintaining the sled and handling cargo
Uneven hair growth pattern on shaved scalp, particularly sparse on left side and back
Dark circles under eyes from habitual light sleep patterns, permanent feature
